note: The source registry (specs/pulse). Adding or removing a source is an ordinary data change, not an OpenSpec change. Every entry records what the source yields, which field is its row id (the join key entries declare in their `feeds` map), its cadences, its robots/terms check, and the date it was last verified live.

frontier.note: The FRONTIER block (specs/pulse, `separate-a-claim-from-a-fact`; DESK-ORDER-001 §4, K24). A published index is somebody else's aggregate, reaching this site through a republisher and read on one day, so it is DECLARED here before any surface reads it: the field name the corpus uses, the path into the source row, the source it is read from, the publisher and its URL, the republisher where the site does not read the publisher directly, which end of the values counts as leading, a display label, and a republication decision. `pulse/lib/frontier.mjs` computes leaders, ranked rows and counts from what is declared here into `data/derived/frontier.json`, and appends a `lead-change` line when a declared metric's leader changes between two consecutive snapshots. NO INDEX VALUE RENDERS until its metric is registered AND its republication decision records the right as CLEARED; a metric that is registered but not cleared is still usable for ordering, for computing a leader and for stating THAT a lead changed. The empty state is a lookup that came back empty, never a hard-wired string.
frontier.metrics_note: EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE DAY-ONE STATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. `separate-a-claim-from-a-fact` states what a registered index must carry and what may not render until it does; it registers no index and clears nobody's terms, which is `verify` work with owners. The two candidates in this feed and where each stands, as recorded on the beads, both OPEN on 2026-09-06: (1) `benchmarks.artificial_analysis.{intelligence,coding,agentic}_index` — addictedtoai-ego8. Artificial Analysis's terms URL 404'd when it was read on 2026-09-05 (DESK-ORDER-001 §4, keeper-signed), so the question is unanswered; the path is additionally recorded in `declined_fields` above as not carried after its own measurement, and a metric declared on a declined path fails this registry loudly, so clearing ego8 means revisiting that refusal in the same edit. (2) `benchmarks.design_arena[]` — addictedtoai-c563, answered but NOT cleared: `field_rights` above records a republication grant with an attribution condition, whose addressee is an API applicant this repository is not and whose attribution condition is unmet. Neither is registered, so `data/derived/frontier.json` carries an empty `metrics` array and the snapshot's own date — the file exists and is looked up, which is the whole point (implementer-ledger row 6: a renderer whose empty state is a constant is a picture of an empty state).
frontier.row_exclusions_note: PATTERNS OVER ROW IDS, NOT FACTS ABOUT THE MODELS. specs/pulse requires rows that are not distinct listed models to be excluded by DECLARED criteria rather than by a rule compiled into the code, so the exclusions are visible and reviewable — and it requires the registry to record that they are patterns. Each row below carries the measurement behind it, taken on `data/sources/openrouter-models/latest.json` (snapshot date 2026-09-05, fetched_at 2026-09-05T06:00:04.599Z, 431 rows). The THIRD category specs/pulse names — alias rows redirecting elsewhere — has NO row below because it has no members here: every `canonical_slug` carried by more than one row id in that snapshot (79 groups) is a `:`-variant pair, and the count of duplicate-slug groups containing more than one non-variant id is ZERO. A pattern that matches nothing is a check that cannot fire, so its absence is recorded here as a measurement rather than declared as a rule.

row_exclusions.reason: service variant of a base row
row_exclusions.note: 88 of the 431 rows carry a ':' suffix — `:batch` on 69 and `:free` on 19 — and 83 of those 88 have their base row present in the same snapshot. They are billing or scheduling variants of a model already listed, not distinct listed models, so counting them would let one model hold several places in a ranking and could hand the lead to a row that is the leader wearing a different price. The measurement that matters is the 83; a variant whose base is absent is rare (5 rows) and is excluded on the same rule rather than a second one, because the pattern is over ids and cannot see why a base is missing.

row_exclusions.reason: router or tool pseudo-row, not a listed model
row_exclusions.note: Six rows in the 2026-09-05 snapshot: `openrouter/auto` and `openrouter/auto-beta` ("The Auto Router automatically selects the best model for your prompt"), `openrouter/free` ("a router that selects free models at random"), `openrouter/fusion` ("turns your prompt into a small multi-model deliberation"), `openrouter/pareto-code` ("maintains a tiered shortlist of strong coding models, ranked by Artificial Analysis coding percentiles") and `openrouter/bodybuilder` ("Transform your natural language requests into structured OpenRouter API request objects"). Each is the platform's own routing or tooling surface over other people's models, so an index value on one is a property of the routing and not of a model — the same confusion implementer-ledger row 10 records from the other side, where a router's measured throughput was admitted as a vendor's own claim. The pattern is over the id prefix and would exclude a model OpenRouter itself published under that prefix; none exists in this snapshot, and the remedy if one appears is a narrower declared pattern here, not a rule in the code.

sources.title: OpenRouter model catalog
sources.material_fields_note: `material_fields` does double duty: it is the CATALOG COLUMN SET (pulse/lib/derive.mjs builds each catalog row from it and skips a source declaring none) and the ENTRY-PAGE FACT SET (pulse/lib/mint.mjs binds one feed fact per spec), and it is also the CHANGED-FEED EVENT SET (pulse/lib/diff.mjs). `event: false` separates the last job from the first two: the column stays, the entry-page fact stays, the feed line stops. Deleting the field would have blanked all three, which is the trap addictedtoai-8ho names.

material_fields.note: A column and a fact, not an event. OpenRouter documents this field as "Pricing from the top provider for this model" — one provider's posted rate, with the top provider re-chosen on a rolling 30-second outage window and inverse-square price weighting. Measured 2026-08-29 across 56 priced models: 55 headline prices exactly equalled one provider endpoint's posted rate (only 4 equalled the arithmetic mean), and the cross-provider spread reached 14.7x. The value is verbatim but the referent rotates, so a movement is a routing artifact, not a repricing — and this repo's own snapshots show the same row falling 10.81% then 10.56% in 20 hours, and another falling and rising back. addictedtoai-8ho.
Same field, same mechanism, same measurement as price_input above. addictedtoai-8ho.

sources.declined_fields_note: The third state `material_fields_note` does not cover. A path in `material_fields` is CARRIED (column + fact, and an event unless `event: false`). A path in neither list is UNDECIDED — nobody has looked, which is what a field looks like when the vendor added it after this entry was written, and it is indistinguishable from a refusal from the outside. This list is the fourth answer to that note's question — column, fact, event, or NONE OF THOSE — recorded rather than left to default. `decision` may only be "not carried": carrying is expressed by `material_fields`, so a `declined_fields` entry claiming otherwise would be a decision written where nothing can enact it. pulse/lib/registry.mjs refuses a path that is both declined and material, and refuses a refusal with no dated measurement behind it. This list ends the undecided state for the paths it names and for no others: 23 further paths this source serves are still in it, and the check that would make the state unreachable is addictedtoai-eexr.

declined_fields.note: Not a column, not a fact, not an event — the same shape of finding as price_input above, and for the same underlying reason: the value is verbatim but the referent moved. Measured 2026-09-05 over all nine committed snapshots in git (data/sources/openrouter-models/latest.json, 2026-08-28 through 2026-09-05). NOT AN EVENT: across the first seven day-boundaries the three indices moved on at most ONE row on any one day; then between the 2026-09-04T06:00:03Z and 2026-09-05T06:00:04Z fetches, 165 of the 179 rows carrying the block changed at once, 147 directional moves went DOWN and 0 went up (agentic_index 97 down / 0 up, intelligence_index 50 down / 0 up), 181 values went number->null with 0 going null->number, and coding_index sat still on 176 of 179. intelligence_index fell by a near-uniform fifth (ratio p25 0.781, median 0.803, p75 0.827). One publisher act, not 165 model facts — and 56 of the carrying row ids are `:batch`/`:free` twins of a canonical_slug already counted, so a per-row line would emit that one act more than once per model. Corroborating but not load-bearing: Artificial Analysis published "Announcing Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.2" (https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/artificial-analysis-intelligence-index-v4-2) dated September 4, 2026, saying "Index v4.2 has more complex and realistic tasks, and more private test sets to prevent gaming"; that article states neither the direction of the shift nor which models were re-run, so the decision rests on the measurement, not on it. NOT A COLUMN: the block is present on 181 of 431 rows (42%), and after the rebase intelligence_index is a number on 52 rows (12%) and agentic_index on 99 (23%). NOT A FACT: the row carries a bare number with no scale, no index version and no measurement date, so the site could not say which index a value belongs to — the 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-05 readings of one key are 20% apart and both would have rendered as "intelligence_index". Binding it would import exactly the rot that "volatile values are bound, never typed" exists to prevent. Revisit if OpenRouter starts serving the index version and evaluation date alongside the number, or if coverage stops collapsing on a rebase.

sources.field_rights_note: A RIGHTS CHECK IS NOT A CARRIAGE DECISION, and this list is separate from the two above so that the difference survives. `material_fields` says a field is carried; `declined_fields` says it is refused after a measurement; this list says what the field's own PUBLISHER permits, in the publisher's words, with the date the documents were read. It is inert data of the same species as `robots` and `verification` below — a dated finding, not a switch — and a path may appear here and in neither of the other two lists, which is what a cleared-but-uncarried field looks like. Recording the rights answer where nothing enacts it is the point: the enacting list is `material_fields`, and moving a path there is a separate decision with its own materiality measurement to make.

field_rights.note: THE ANSWER IS YES-WITH-A-CONDITION, AND THE CONDITION IS NOT MET TODAY, WHICH IS WHY THIS CHANGES NOTHING THAT RENDERS. Design Arena's developer documentation carries an explicit grant — data from its API is "free to use for personal and commercial projects" — and attaches one requirement to any public display: credit Design Arena and show a visible link to designarena.ai. So the rights question DESK-ORDER-001 §4 left open has an answer, and the answer is not a refusal. Two things stop it short of clearance, and both are stated rather than argued. FIRST, THE ADDRESSEE. The grant is scoped to "data from the Design Arena API", an API whose overview says "All API requests require authentication using a Bearer token" and whose key is issued only on an application where step 2 is "Describe your use case and agree to the attribution requirements"; the grant's own closing sentence is "By applying for API access, you agree to these attribution requirements." This repository holds no key, has never fetched designarena.ai for data, and reads these values third-hand out of OpenRouter's `benchmarks.design_arena` block. No fetched document says whether the grant reaches a party who never applied, and applying for one is an outward-facing act with a named human on it — the maintainer's, not a job's. SECOND, THE TERMS PULL THE OTHER WAY WHERE THEY SPEAK AT ALL. The Terms of Service (Last Updated: June 7, 2026) contain no republication grant, claim exclusive ownership of "Service Information" — defined in §7 as "data, derived or aggregated in deidentified form, from such User Content or from your use of the Services", which is what an Elo computed from user votes is — and prohibit displaying "any individual element within the Services" without express written consent and using "the Services, or any portion thereof, for any commercial purpose". Those clauses govern use of the Site and App and are silent about data received from a third party, so they do not contradict the docs' grant so much as decline to extend it. robots.txt allows crawling everything except /api/ and /admin/, which is consistent and not load-bearing: nothing here crawls Design Arena. WHAT IS IN THE FEED, measured 2026-09-05 on data/sources/openrouter-models/latest.json (fetched_at 2026-09-05T06:00:04.599Z, 431 rows): 243 rows carry a `benchmarks.design_arena` key and 165 of those carry a NON-EMPTY array — the 165 DESK-ORDER-001 §4 names is the non-empty count, and the 78 empty arrays are the difference. 1,577 entries in all, across 25 arena/category pairs over two arenas (`models`, `agents`), each entry `{arena, category, elo, rank, win_rate}`, spanning 120 distinct canonical_slugs. The pair count has been 25 in every committed snapshot from 2026-08-28 to 2026-09-05 and the non-empty row count rose 148 → 165 over those nine days. NOTHING RENDERS TODAY AND NOTHING IN THIS ENTRY MAKES ANYTHING RENDER: the path is absent from `yields` and from `material_fields`, so no catalog column, entry-page fact or changed-feed line exists for it, and a full `npm run build` on 2026-09-05, scanned exhaustively over all 1,412 files and 32,009,793 bytes of `out/`, emitted the tokens `design_arena`, `designarena`, `Design Arena`, `DesignArena` and `winRate` zero times each. `win_rate` occurs 19 times in 6 files and none of them is this feed: they are the hand-authored cited facts `technique/proximal-policy-optimization#win_rate` (an InstructGPT preference rate quoted from arXiv 2203.02155) and `event/alphago-lee-sedol#cyclic_adversary_win_rate`, reported here rather than filtered away because a scan that reports only what suits the conclusion is not a measurement. The values do sit verbatim inside `data/derived/feed-rows.json`, which is a committed derived file and not a served one. WHAT WOULD CLEAR IT, in order: an API key applied for by the maintainer (or a written statement from Arcada Labs that the grant covers relayed data), and an attribution mechanism that renders the credit and the visible link beside every value, since the grant's condition is about display and a value displayed without it is a breach rather than a defect. Only then is the materiality question — is a bare Elo with no scale, no date and no index version a column, a fact or an event — worth asking; it is the same question the `benchmarks.artificial_analysis` refusal above answered no to, on measurements that do not automatically transfer. Evidence: data/reviews/evidence/verify-design-arena-republication-terms.md and its .raw.txt transcript, job j-20260905-24.

status_rule.note: OpenRouter serves no status field of its own. Status is derived deterministically from `expiration_date`: absent -> active; in the past -> retired; within 365 days -> deprecated; further out -> active. The far-future sentinel dates the API carries (2098-12-31 on several z-ai rows, observed 2026-08-28) therefore read as active, which is what they mean — deriving `deprecated` from a sentinel would fire a false lifecycle timeline event on the joined entry.

radar_note: THE SCOUT'S RADAR FEEDS, AND THEY ARE NOT SOURCES. `sources` above is what the Pulse fetches, snapshots, diffs and derives from; every row of it can reach a rendered page. `radar` is DESK-ORDER-001 §5 / keeper ruling K30: feeds the scout reads to decide where to look, which this engine never fetches and which never render. They are a separate array rather than a flagged source because a flag would have to be honoured by every consumer that iterates `sources` — run.mjs, derive.mjs, mint.mjs, diff.mjs, freshness.mjs and whatever is written next — and one that forgets it would silently ingest and publish a radar feed. Measured: derive.mjs writes every `sources[]` row's id, title and url into data/derived/sources.json BEFORE the material_fields check that skips catalog rows, and lib/data-layer.mjs feeds that file to lib/site.mjs, so `material_fields: []` does not keep a row off the site. Nothing iterating `registry.sources` can reach these rows at all; pulse/lib/registry.mjs `radarFeeds()` and `radarReadableUrls()` are the only way in. Each row records robots, terms and a last-verified date, as §5 requires, and a URL a site forbids is recorded as refused and never handed to a caller.

robots.detail: THE OBVIOUS URL IS THE FORBIDDEN ONE. github.com/robots.txt (HTTP 200, 2,274 bytes, fetched 2026-09-06) contains, inside its `User-agent: *` group, the line "Disallow: /*.atom$". That pattern matches https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases.atom exactly, so the releases Atom feed — the URL DESK-ORDER-001 §5's phrasing points at — is disallowed for every crawler. It answers anyway: one probe of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases.atom on 2026-09-06 returned HTTP 200 and 512,052 bytes of application/atom+xml. That probe was made once, before the robots file had been read, and is recorded rather than hidden; it will not be repeated and no .atom URL is registered. HTTP 200 is not permission. The same group also disallows /*/*/tags, /*/*/commits/ and /*/tree/. WHAT THE FILE POINTS AT INSTEAD, in its own second line: "# We also provide an extensive API: https://docs.github.com". api.github.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 404 with the body {"message": "Not Found", "documentation_url": "https://docs.github.com/rest", "status": "404"} — no robots file on that host, so nothing there is disallowed.
